tokyo_dontatsu_suidobashi_pork.price_note: The shop publishes its whole card on one page and it is short: five bowls and a challenge. Rice is oversized by default — 「丼達のご飯は並でも大盛りサイズ」 — and the shop will make a 小盛り for 50円 off if you ask, which is worth knowing because this is a 大食い (competitive-eating) landmark near Tokyo Dome and the standard portion is not standard. Toppings are ordered in the shop rather than listed with prices; the shop names 生たまご, バター and 温玉 as the usual ones. ⚠ THE ENTIRE SAVOURY CARD IS SOY-BASED AND THAT IS THE WHOLE COELIAC STORY HERE. Each pork bowl is sold with a choice of four sauces — てりやきにんにく, てりやきしょうが, 醤油ピリ辛 and 塩しょうが — and three of the four are named for soy: teriyaki is soy, mirin and sugar, and 醤油ピリ辛 is soy by definition. Japanese soy sauce is wheat-brewed unless it is declared tamari, and the shop declares nothing. ⚠ THE ONE INTERESTING LINE IS 塩しょうが, THE SALT-AND-GINGER SAUCE. A salt-ginger dressing is the only one of the four whose name does not contain soy, and the same idea appears again in ねぎ塩豚丼 at 850円, a spring-onion-and-salt bowl. On a card where everything else is teriyaki, a shio-based sauce is the one thing worth asking about — but it is recorded ask rather than gf, because Japanese 塩だれ is very often built on a base that still includes soy or dashi, and the shop publishes no ingredients at all. ⚠ 丼達カレー at 920円 is a flat no regardless: Japanese curry is thickened with a wheat-flour roux. And 鶏そぼろ丼 is minced chicken simmered in soy. ⚠ FOR A VEGAN THERE IS NOTHING HERE — five bowls, all pork, chicken or a meat curry, with no vegetable option printed.

tokyo_asakusa_unana.price_note: The shop's own お品書き page carries a price against every line and repeats the whole board twice — once as a picture-menu grid and once as a plain 一覧 list. The two agree except on one figure, and the disagreement is recorded here rather than smoothed over: うなぎ蒲焼 竹 is 1,980円 in the grid and 2,980円 in the list, which straddles the 松 price of 2,540円 in one direction and sits sensibly between 梅 and 松 in the other. The grid figure of 1,980円 is the one consistent with the 松/竹/梅 ladder, so it is recorded as the price with the conflict flagged; do not treat either number as settled. Run by 浅草麦酒合同会社 at 東京都台東区浅草2-7-21. ⚠ THIS IS A GRILLED-EEL SHOP AND KABAYAKI TARE IS THE WHOLE POINT OF IT: every eel item is lacquered in a soy-sauce-and-mirin glaze, which makes the entire eel half of the board wheat by default, and eel itself rules out vegan. ⚠ THE ONE ITEM THAT LOOKS LIKE AN EXCEPTION IS NOT ONE — the 焼きおにぎり at 630円 is a rice ball, but it is an EEL rice ball basted on the grill, so it carries both the fish and the soy. There is nothing on this board for either diet.

tokyo_fleur_de_sarrasin.price_note: ⚠ THIS RECORD CARRIES A GLUTEN-FREE CLAIM IN THE DATASET AND THE SHOP'S OWN SITE DOES NOT MAKE ONE — read that before anything else. Fleur de Sarrasin is a ガレットと国産シードル専門店, a buckwheat-galette and Japanese-cider specialist, and buckwheat is not wheat, which is presumably where the cuisine label came from. But NOTHING on the shop's own Menu page says gluten-free, says 100% buckwheat, or says the flour is unblended. Most Japanese galette kitchens work alongside a wheat crêpe, and the shop's own Dinner list opens with 蕎麦チップス and そば味噌 in the same breath as 生ハム and チョリソー off a shared counter. Worse for a coeliac specifically: the shop states 「日祝の夜は蕎麦生地がなくなり次第閉店」 — it closes when the buckwheat batter runs out — which tells you the batter is made in one daily quantity and tells you nothing about what is in it. EVERY GALETTE BELOW IS THEREFORE 'ask', NOT 'gf'. Even 十割 soba means 打ち粉 and shared water, and the site never claims 十割 in the first place. ⚠ THE PRICES ARE FROM-PRICES AND THE MENU IS DELIBERATELY OPEN-ENDED: 前菜 490〜, 黒ガレット 1,500〜, 白ガレット 890〜, each followed by an example list ending in etc…, so the published card is a shape rather than a complete board. Weekday lunch 黒 1,990 and 黒と白 2,590; holiday lunch サラザン 2,990 with the shop noting the contents change by season; a 7-dish share course at 4,990 per person from two people, and a cider-pairing version of it at 9,990. Hours 11:45–15:00 (L.O. 14:00) and 17:45–23:00 (L.O. 21:00), irregular closing. ⚠ THE ONE GENUINELY GOOD VEGAN LEAD IS THE 白ガレット, whose example fillings include きな粉、黒蜜、抹茶アイス — soy flour and brown-sugar syrup are plants, but the 抹茶アイス next to them is not, and the default white galette is 北海道よつ葉有塩バター. Ask for the kinako-and-kuromitsu build without the ice cream.

tokyo_jimjum_jim_jum_2.price_note: PARTIAL, AND THE MISSING HALF IS THE PRICES. JIMJUM's own WordPress site has a four-page menu section, but the boards themselves are POSTED AS PHOTOGRAPHS — the lunch page is a wall of JPEGs with no alt text and no transcription, so not one lunch price is recoverable from it. The dinner page is better only because the shop typed dish names as captions under its photos, and those captions are the item list below; no price appears anywhere on it either. Everything recorded here is a dish the shop names in its own text. Nothing is priced, and nothing has been guessed. What the site does say in words: hours are lunch 11:30–14:00 on weekdays except Thursday and 11:30–15:00 at weekends, dinner 18:00–23:00 on weekdays and 17:30–23:00 at weekends, last orders 30 minutes before each; closed Mondays; 東京都台東区浅草1-43-8 原田ビル2F, tel 03-3841-8806. The lunch page adds in text that the popular Thai curries are red, massaman (yellow) and green 「のほか色々」, and warns that items go off the board when they sell out or when Thai ingredients cannot be sourced. ⚠ THAI FOOD IS THE CUISINE WHERE 'NO WHEAT VISIBLE' IS MOST MISLEADING: fish sauce (ナンプラー) and shrimp paste (カピ) are in the base of nearly everything including the curry pastes and the som tam dressing, which makes most of this board a VEGAN problem long before it is a gluten one, and oyster sauce and soy sauce carry the wheat on the stir-fries. ⚠ AND THE TWO KHAO SOI BOWLS ARE THE HARD NO: khao soi is an EGG-NOODLE dish, wheat by construction, and it is conventionally topped with a second helping of the same noodles deep-fried.

tokyo_soba_ju.price_note: SOBA-JU publishes its board on its own single-page site in three blocks — 蕎麦 SOBA (11:30–14:30), 一品料理 DINNER (18:00–25:00) and 飲み物 DRINK — with a price against every line, and closes two of the three blocks with 「...etc.」 and the caveat 「メニューは季節のおすすめをご用意しておりますので、替わる場合がございます」, so what is below is the published board rather than the whole board. ⚠ THE SAME DISH IS PRICED TWICE AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE TIME OF DAY: 肉蕎麦 is ￥1,100 at lunch and ￥1,300 at night, and both figures are recorded rather than reconciled. Fifteen counter seats, 東京都新宿区新宿3-10-1 吉岡ビル1階, tel 03-6380-1705, lunch Mon–Sat, dinner Tue–Sat, closed Sunday. It is part of the MARUGO group and the site warns that the group has several similarly named shops, so a booking can land at the wrong one. ⚠ THIS IS A SOBA SHOP AND ALMOST NOTHING ABOUT IT IS GLUTEN-FREE, WHICH IS WORTH SAYING PLAINLY BECAUSE 'soba' IS THE WORD THAT MOST OFTEN GETS A COELIAC INTO TROUBLE IN JAPAN. The shop's own CONCEPT text names its noodle as 挽きぐるみ極太平打ち麺 — a coarse wholemeal-grind, extra-thick flat noodle — and says nothing at all about the buckwheat ratio. A noodle described only by its grind and its cut is a 二八 or looser blend by default, i.e. roughly 20% wheat, and even 十割 would still mean 打ち粉 and shared boiling water. The tsuyu compounds it: the shop describes it as カエシ (soy-sauce base) with sabá, so the broth is wheat and fish in the same sentence. ⚠ AND THE VEGAN SIDE IS WORSE THAN THE GLUTEN SIDE: the entire noodle section is beef, pork or duck, the dinner block is offal, sashimi and sukiyaki, and the one plant dish on the card — 季節野菜のお浸し — is an ohitashi, which is by definition vegetables steeped in dashi.

tokyo_otaco_otako_chiffon_cake.price_note: ⚠ THIS SHOP MAKES THE STRONGEST FIRST-PARTY GLUTEN STATEMENT IN THE TOKYO SET AND IT IS WORTH QUOTING EXACTLY. On its own home, about and shop pages otaco writes: 「otacoは、米粉のシフォンケーキの専門店です。小麦粉は厨房にも一切置いておりませんので、gluten freeのお客さまも安心して召し上がれます。」 — *there is no wheat flour in the kitchen at all*. That is not 'we have a gluten-free option': it is a claim that the flour is absent from the premises, which is the thing that actually matters for cross-contact and the thing almost no Japanese bakery says. The about page then names the four ingredients it is built on: domestic 米粉 (rice flour, which the shop notes is additive-free and about 5% lower in calories than wheat flour), 菜種油 pressed from domestic rapeseed by the traditional 玉締め method with no chemical solvents, 奥久慈卵 eggs from a farm in Ibaraki (the shop says the supplier can change with the season), and きび砂糖, unrefined cane sugar boiled down mid-refining. ⚠ AND THE SAME PAGE THAT MAKES IT SAFE FOR A COELIAC RULES IT OUT FOR A VEGAN, IN THE SHOP'S OWN WORDS: 「シフォンケーキのふくらみは卵のメレンゲの力！」 — the rise IS the egg meringue. There is no leavening here other than whipped egg white, so a vegan version is not a substitution away; it is a different cake. This is the cleanest example in the dataset of the two axes being independent. ⚠ NOTHING IS PRICED AND THERE IS NO FLAVOUR LIST, BECAUSE THE PRODUCT PAGE IS DOWN: otaco-sweets.com/shop/ currently reads 「ただいまメンテナンス中です」 and directs enquiries to chiffon@otaco-sweets.com. The blog also states that current information now goes to Instagram (chiffon_cake_otaco) rather than the site. So the record below is one item — the thing the shop exists to sell — with the gluten and vegan facts attached, and no invented flavours or figures. 〒111-0032 東京都台東区浅草3-5-1, tel/fax 03-6458-1375, eight minutes' walk from Asakusa station and three from the Sensō-ji main hall.

items.ja: 米粉のシフォンケーキ
items.section: シフォンケーキ Chiffon cake
items.note: ⚠ GLUTEN-FREE ON THE SHOP'S OWN EXPLICIT CLAIM, NOT ON INFERENCE: otaco states that wheat flour is not kept in the kitchen at all and that gluten-free customers can eat here with confidence. Built on domestic rice flour, solvent-free traditional-pressed rapeseed oil, Okukuji eggs and unrefined kibi cane sugar. ⚠ NOT VEGAN AND CANNOT BE MADE SO — the shop says outright that the cake's rise is the egg meringue, so egg is the structure rather than an ingredient that could be swapped. No flavours or prices are published; the product page is under maintenance and the shop points customers to Instagram and to chiffon@otaco-sweets.com.

tokyo_d_i_y_salad_delicatessen.price_note: EMPTY, AND THE PDF WAS DOWNLOADED AND CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The operator (ADemotion / cardenas.co.jp) gives the shop a brand page with a MENU/PLAN block whose 'REGULAR MENU' link points at 202607_B1_BLF_1ol.pdf. That file is 1.9 MB, it downloads fine, and pdftotext extracts ONE BYTE from it — it is a flattened image scan with no text layer at all. That is a finding, not a failure: the menu exists, it is published, and it is not machine-readable. The brand page's own prose is all that can be quoted: a salad-and-deli shop built on チョップドサラダ (chopped salads) with デリプレート that include a substantial amount of meat, positioned as an all-day option, and two footnotes worth carrying — 「内容は変更されている場合があります」 and 「お米は国産ブレンド米を使用しています」, the rice is a domestic blend. 〒160-0023 東京都新宿区西新宿1-1-5 ルミネ新宿1 B2F, tel 03-6304-5774, 11:00–21:00 (L.O. 20:30). ⚠ WORTH A SECOND LOOK WITH OCR, BECAUSE THIS IS EXACTLY THE KIND OF SHOP THAT COULD SERVE BOTH DIETS AND MIGHT SERVE NEITHER: a build-your-own chopped salad counter is one of the few formats in Shinjuku where a vegan can actually assemble a meal, and the whole question turns on the DRESSINGS and on whether the deli plates share tongs with the salad bar — neither of which the readable part of the site addresses. Recorded empty so the queue stops re-selecting it.

tokyo_rec_coffee_suidobashi.price_note: Prices are read from REC COFFEE's own menu PDF, reached via the "View Menu" button on the Suidobashi shop page itself — so it is this branch's card, not a generic chain page. The shop page also gives the address 3-10-1 Kanda Misakicho, Chiyoda-ku, hours Mon–Fri 7:30–20:00 and weekends/holidays 9:00–19:00, a morning menu served until 10:00, 30 seats, and guide dogs only. HOW THESE PRICES WERE READ, BECAUSE IT MATTERS: the PDF is a four-column single page, and a flat text extraction mis-paired several drinks with the wrong prices (it put ESPRESSO BANANA SHAKE at 800/950, which is actually COFFEE FLOAT). The values below come from a column-preserving extraction that is internally consistent across all four columns. Where a drink has two prices they are Regular / Large. The PDF's Japanese text is in Adobe-Japan1 CID fonts that did not extract, so the ja field below carries the katakana/Japanese name only where it is unambiguous from the English; nothing was invented. ⚠ WHAT A COELIAC NEEDS TO KNOW HERE: this is a specialty coffee bar, so the drinks side is mostly low-risk by form — but REC publishes NO allergen statement at all, and the food side is entirely bread (sandwich, hot dog, three toasts). A toaster and a counter shared with bread is the cross-contamination surface, and it is the reason the plain drinks below are recorded as ask rather than gf despite being coffee and juice. There IS a genuinely useful fact for a vegan traveller: the customise row prints OATS MILK as a paid option (+120 Regular / +160 Large), so every milk drink here can be made dairy-free on request. DECAF is +100.
